pipeline.modality: Anthracycline chemotherapy (small molecule) — first anthracycline reported to cross the blood-brain barrier
pipeline.target: Topoisomerase II (induces DNA damage in proliferating cells)
pipeline.license_origin: In-licensed (legacy asset, originally Reata Pharmaceuticals/Houston Pharmaceuticals)

indications.indication: Recurrent glioblastoma multiforme (GBM, WHO grade IV) after first-line failure
indications.trial_name: CNS-201 — potentially pivotal Phase 2 of Berubicin vs lomustine in adult recurrent GBM
indications.trial_design: Randomized, controlled Phase 2 superiority trial; Berubicin vs lomustine comparator; 252-patient enrollment completed; primary endpoint overall survival.
indications.trial_status: ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING per ctgov; per 10-K (filed Mar 2026) the trial did not meet primary endpoint at primary analysis; current plan is to complete trial, close sites and prepare CSR; company is exploring out-licensing rather than further internal development.
key_milestones: Primary analysis (H1 2025): outcomes appeared comparable to lomustine but did not meet superiority primary endpoint.
March 2026: corporate strategy pivot — exploring out-licensing of Berubicin and TPI 287; pursuing acquisitions in neurology/oncology.
Fast Track Designation (2021) and Orphan Drug Designation for malignant gliomas.

excluded_legacy_terminated: TPI 287 (abeotaxane) — legacy in-licensed asset evaluated in prior Phase 1/2 (sponsor-investigator/external) studies; no active Company-sponsored trial; out-licensing being explored.
no_active_clinical_pipeline_reason: Company has pivoted strategy in March 2026 to out-licensing legacy assets (Berubicin, TPI 287); only one active Phase 2 trial remains and is winding down with negative readout. New growth strategy targets acquisitions in neurology/oncology not yet executed.
